text:
sales-ian: Hey team — GoldStripe POC. Customer reports TTFT spike and intermittent 429s during demo. Median first-token latency ~3.8s (expected ~1.2s). Need a quick swarm to root-cause and keep the deal moving. Can we triage now? :warning:

alex: On it. Which model + runtime config are they using? Any client concurrency patterns?

maria: They ran rwd-13b-quant, batching_strategy=auto, client parallelism ~12 connections, batch_size=8, max_tokens=512, kv_cache=true, region=us-east-1. Using streaming in the client but still high TTFT.

eng-oncall: I pulled the proxy logs — seeing a burst of 429s around 10:14:57 and then sustained high p50 TTFT. Snippet below:

```
[2026-03-19T10:14:57Z] request_id=aa1f user=goldstripe key=gs-poc status=429 reason=concurrency_limit_exceeded
[2026-03-19T10:14:58Z] request_id=aa20 user=goldstripe model=rwd-13b-quant ttft_ms=3870 cache_hit=false
[2026-03-19T10:15:01Z] request_id=aa28 user=goldstripe status=200 ttft_ms=1180 batch_size=6 cache_hit=true
[2026-03-19T10:15:05Z] request_id=aa39 user=goldstripe status=429 reason=rate_limit_per_key
```

eng-oncall: Also saw many cache_miss=true lines — KV cache hit rate ~18% for this window.

alex: Two likely pain points: client-side concurrency exceeding per-key concurrency cap -> 429s and excessive cache misses causing cold starts and longer per-token compute.

maria: Agree. Their prompts include user-scoped metadata per request (user_id, session_uuid) which likely invalidates prefix caching.

alex: Suggested quick fixes to try right away:
- reduce client concurrency to 4-6 connections temporarily
- set batching_strategy=latency_p95 or fixed batch_size=4 to avoid creating large batches that delay first token
- enable prefix_whitelist + normalize prompt templates (remove user_id from cache key)
- temporarily increase per-key concurrency quota for the POC (sales -> eng-ops)
- if immediate SLA needed, route this key to a dedicated pool with reserved capacity

maria: Small config we tested locally: batching_strategy=fixed, batch_size=4, kv_cache_key_template="{{prompt_normalized}}" — reduced local TTFT from 2.6s -> 1.1s on similar workload.

eng-oncall: I'll open a quota escalation ticket and attach logs. @josh can you approve short-term quota bump for the demo window?

josh: I can approve a temporary bump for the demo — patching quotas now. Will follow up with rev & proposal for dedicated pricing.

security-eva: Quick flag on security questionnaire from GoldStripe: they asked whether we log raw prompts and whether PII is stored. For the POC we should enable prompt redaction and set logs to minimal retention.

alex: Agreed — for the POC instruct client to mask user ids; on the service side we can set prompt_redaction=true and log_level=error, retention=7d.

maria: Action items:
- alex -> push config change with batching_strategy=fixed, batch_size=4 and new cache_key template, test in staging (15m)
- eng-oncall -> escalate per-key concurrency quota and monitor 429s (10m)
- josh -> approve quota bump & follow-up with dedicated pricing delta (send numbers)
- security-eva -> confirm redaction settings and update security response (20m)

sre-bot: Canary routing rule applied to gs-poc key -> routed to dedicated-pool-2 for next 30m.

sales-ian: Thanks all — we're on the call with GoldStripe at :30. Please update here when changes are live.

alex: Making change now and will post measurements in ~10 mins. :rocket:

maria: Also sending a quick doc snippet to GoldStripe about prompt normalization and a templating example.

eng-oncall: Update: quota bump applied; 429s dropped to near-zero, cache hit rate slowly improving to ~42% after normalization. TTFT median down to ~1.2s in the last 3m.

sales-ian: Amazing. Marking this POC as back on track. I'll request a short case study and next-steps call. :tada:
